name: Yahboom ROSMASTER
description: A family of ROS/ROS2 educational and research robot kits from Yahboom, spanning eight active models — from the $300 Ackermann-steered A1 up to the $1,400+ M3 Pro with a 6-DOF arm and dual lidar. This catalog entry represents the whole ROSMASTER line as one product family rather than eight separate pages; the photo shown is specifically the base ROSMASTER X3, a mecanum-drive SLAM/navigation kit.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: 6000mAh pack; short next to some competitors per reviewers

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: varies by model across the 8-SKU lineup; no reliable single figure found in this research

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.note: varies by model across the 8-SKU lineup; no reliable single figure found in this research

specs.label: Sensors
specs.note: YDLidar or "SLAM A1" lidar; Astra/Astra Pro depth camera

specs.label: Compute
specs.note: each model offers multiple compute-board tiers

specs.label: Software
specs.note: older X3 also supports ROS1 Melodic; Nav2 + Cartographer SLAM

specs.label: Drive
specs.note: varies by model — A1/R2/R2L steer, X3/M1/M3 are omnidirectional

specs.label: Lineup
specs.note: A1, M1, R2, R2L, X3, X3 Plus, M3, M3 Pro

specs.label: Arm Option
specs.note: X3 Plus and M3 Pro add a robotic arm; base X3/M3 do not

specs.label: Price Range
specs.note: A1 cheapest; M3 Pro's top configuration most expensive

sourcing: Verified against Yahboom's official ROSMASTER collection page and individual product pages for A1, M1, R2, R2L, X3, X3 Plus, M3, and M3 Pro; the YahboomTechnology GitHub organization and per-model repositories (including star/fork counts and Nav2/Cartographer configuration files); DOFBOT's separate official product page and GitHub repo (confirming it is not part of the ROSMASTER line); independent educator AutomaticAddison's public Nav2 tutorial repo built on a physical ROSMASTER X3; a university robotics club's (AIRclub-UdeSA) public coursework repos; a hobbyist-robotics forum thread discussing Yahboom's documentation and support quality; and RobotShop and OpenELAB distributor/education listings. Flagged as uncertain: R2L's exact standalone price (not separately listed at research time); precise top-configuration pricing for X3 Plus and M3 Pro once every compute-board option is factored in; and whether any ROSMASTER repository carries a formal open-source license, which this catalog could not confirm from the repos' visible files.

pricing.summary: Pricing spans the widest range of any single entry in this catalog, because it covers eight distinct SKUs: ROSMASTER A1 from $299.90, M1 from $349.90, R2 around $655, X3 around $659, M3 from $779.90 (list $1,809.90), X3 Plus from $1,229 (list $1,729), and M3 Pro from $1,444 (list $2,034) — with R2L positioned as a stripped-down, lower-cost variant of R2 not separately listed at a fixed price. Sold through Yahboom's own storefront (category.yahboom.net, primary source for current pricing), RobotShop, Amazon, and AliExpress, with per-model pricing that swings further depending on which compute board (Raspberry Pi 5 vs. a top-tier Jetson Orin NX Super module) is selected at checkout.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Each ROSMASTER model has a real, actively-starred GitHub repository under Yahboom's official organization, but license files are not clearly present in these repos, so this entry is not tagged open source — the code is public but not formally licensed.

firmwareCommunity.note: Yahboom's official GitHub repo for ROSMASTER X3 has real Nav2/Cartographer code with meaningful community activity (~99 stars), though it carries no LICENSE file, so usage rights are not formally granted.
